items.title: The determinant lines $\lambda(E)$, $\lambda^*(E)$ and the maps $\lambda(\Phi)$

book.label: §6.3 (preprint §6.2), pp. 241–243 (preprint pp. 203–204)
book.statement: $\lambda(E) = \Lambda^{\max}E$ and $\lambda^*(E) = (\lambda(E))^*$. For $\Phi : E \to F$ between spaces of the same dimension, $\lambda(\Phi)(a_1 \wedge \dots \wedge a_n) = \Phi(a_1) \wedge \dots \wedge \Phi(a_n)$, nontrivial iff $\Phi$ is an isomorphism, with $\lambda(\Psi \circ \Phi) = \lambda(\Psi) \circ \lambda(\Phi)$; $\lambda^*(\Phi)$ is the dual of $\lambda(\Phi)$. The dual vector $v^*$ of $v \ne 0$ in a line is fixed by $v^*(v) = 1$ (preprint p. 204).

lean.statement: `maxPow E`, the top exterior power of a finite-dimensional real space, is a line (`finrank_maxPow`), and `maxPowDual E` is its dual. A change of basis multiplies the `wedge` by the determinant (`wedge_eq_det_smul`), also in one block of a two-block wedge (`wedge_append_basis_left`, `wedge_append_basis_right`), and adding to one block vectors of the span of the other does not change the wedge (`wedge_append_add_left`, `wedge_append_add_right`). `dualVec v` is the functional with $v^*(v) = 1$. For $\dim E = \dim F$, `maxPowMap` is $\lambda(\Phi)$ on wedges (`maxPowMap_wedge`), with $\lambda(\Psi\Phi) = \lambda(\Psi)\lambda(\Phi)$ (`maxPowMap_comp`), nonzero iff $\Phi$ is bijective (`maxPowMap_ne_zero_iff`); `maxPowDualMap` is its dual.

items.title: Theorem 6.6.18 (preprint 6.41): the natural orientation of the solution set

book.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), Theorem 6.6.18 (preprint 6.41) and its proof, preprint p. 229; the paragraph after it, pp. 274–276 (preprint pp. 229–230)
book.statement: Over a tame $X$, for a proper sc-Fredholm section $f$ with $(f, x)$ in general position to $\partial X$ at every zero and an orientation $o^f$ of $f$, the solution set $S = f^{-1}(0)$ is a smooth compact manifold with boundary with corners with a natural orientation. Proof: $T_xS = \ker f'(x)$ is oriented by $o^f_x$ since $f'(x)$ is onto, and the local prolongation of this orientation on $S$ is the Fredholm one. For $f$ not generic, a small perturbation $s$ supported near the zero set orients $S_{f+s}$.

In Mathlib's language $S$ is a compact `IsManifold (modelWithCornersEuclideanQuadrant d) ∞` (`theorem_6_6_18_isManifold`). As a Mathlib manifold $S$ carries the natural orientation (`theorem_6_6_18_oriented`, `Chapter6/SolutionSetOrientation.lean`): a tangent orientation of the Mathlib manifold $S$ of `theorem_6_6_18_isManifold`, continuous in every chart of the maximal atlas (`TangentOrientation.IsContinuous`, `Chapter6/ManifoldOrientation.lean`), such that at every zero $x$ and in every chart of $X$ at $x$ the tangent map of $S \hookrightarrow X$ (`derivIn`) is an isomorphism $T_xS \cong \ker f'(x)$ under which a basis is positive iff its image is positive for $o_x$. The perturbation paragraph: an orientation of $f$ is one of $f + s$ (`isSectionOrientation_sectionAdd`, with $\mathrm{Lin}(f + s, x) = \mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$), so $S_{f+s}$ is oriented by it (`theorem_6_6_18_sectionAdd`), for the dense set of perturbations of Theorem 5.3.10 (preprint 5.18) (`theorem_6_6_18_perturbation`). The forms first recorded: `theorem_6_6_18_solutionSet` ($X$ tame, $f$ with tame germ data, `StrongBundle.IsProper`, general position (Definition 5.3.9 (preprint 5.17)) at every zero): $S$ is compact, a smooth submanifold in general position with the induced structure of a tame manifold with boundary with corners (the conclusions of Theorem 5.3.10 (preprint 5.18); Lemma 4.2.8 (preprint 4.19) for good position, `MPolyfold.IsGeneralPositionAt.isGoodPositionAt`), and $T_xS = \ker f'(x)$ in a chart (`tangentSpace_solutionSet_eq_linKer`). The Fredholm side is the push-forward for the datum $S = 0$, $k = 0$ (`isStabKernels_zero`, `stabSign_of_surjective`, `stabRayEquiv_zero`), which along a path of zeros is the continuation between tangent orientations (`IsStabKernels.orRay_eq_tangentOr`, `ChartPoint.stabRayEquiv_eq_tangentOr`, `cont_tangentOr`).

The orientation of $S$ as a manifold is formalized: a continuous tangent orientation of the Mathlib manifold $S$ which at every zero is $o_x$ transported along the tangent map of $S \hookrightarrow X$ (`theorem_6_6_18_oriented`; gap G.67 closed). The forms first recorded are kept (`theorem_6_6_18_solutionSet`, `theorem_6_6_18_hyp`) (Findings, Chapter 6, items 92, 93, 123).

"A natural orientation" is read as the tangent orientations with their continuity along the sc-smooth paths of zeros in a chart, and "the local prolongation of the orientation on $S$ is the Fredholm one" as the identity of continuation and push-forward along such paths; intermediate points are reached by the paths $s \mapsto \gamma(t\kappa(s))$, which stay in $\gamma([0, t])$ (Findings, Chapter 6, item 91).

The solution set of an admissible section splits into the clopen index parts $S_k$ (`solPart`, `solutionSet_eq_iUnion_solPart`), each a compact (when $S_{f+s}$ is) Mathlib manifold of dimension $k$, oriented by $o$ (`solPartIsOrientedManifold`, `theorem_6_6_18_oriented_open`). The facts recalled are formalized: Theorem 5.3.10 (preprint 5.18) (V5.38, V5.39) and the tangent orientations of the solution set (V6.61); the orientation of $S_{f+s}$ for a perturbed $f$ is gap G.69 (Findings, Chapter 6, item 101). (2026-11-09) Gap G.69 is closed: an orientation of $f$ is one of $f + s$, so it orients $S_{f+s}$ for the perturbations of Theorem 5.3.10 (`theorem_6_6_18_perturbation`, V6.61).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 6.6.17 (2) without connected smooth neighbourhoods
notFormalized.label: §6.6, Theorem 6.6.17 (2), p. 275 (new in the 2021 edition)

notFormalized.title: The remarks after Theorem 6.6.17: the orientation bundle, orientability, $\mathbb Z_2$ and $\det_f$
